existingReportSummary.executiveSummaryMd: Encounter has high-impact local breaking changes despite stable identity. Top concerns are required status code changes, structural remodels for class/reason/diagnosis/participants/timing, and lossy R6-to-R4 conversion. Main uncertainty is official migration intent for histories and terminology.
existingReportSummary.migrationThemesMd: Implement explicit transforms for status, class, actual/planned timing, admission, participant actor, reason, diagnosis, serviceType, and location form. Preserve removed history/rank data deliberately and define R6-to-R4 extension or rejection rules.
existingReportSummary.confidenceSummaryMd: Confidence is high for StructureDefinition deltas and local complete status CodeSystems. Confidence is medium for terminology semantics and replacement intent because official diffs, narrative pages, and terminology expansions were not available.

compatibilityLeverage.note: Resource-level leverage is a planning signal. It does not mark individual Revisit findings as justified or unimportant.

rationaleMd:
Encounter keeps its resource identity. The aggregate has 11 hard R4-to-R6 instance break(s), 0 potential hard break(s), 8 non-mechanical migration finding(s), and 6 direct behavior/API finding(s).

R4 maturity context is trial-use/FMM 2, which creates neutral stability pressure.

The computed migration-unavoidability score is 100/100, producing migration shape `major-model-remodel`, major migration `Yes`, and compatibility posture `preserve-where-low-cost-but-expect-resource-migration`.

10 finding(s) identify a yes/partial less-breaking base-design alternative, so the aggregate should not be used to dismiss local avoidability review.

10 shared Resource/DomainResource behavior finding(s) are listed as context but not scored for this resource to avoid duplicating base behavior issues across all resources.
recommendedStandardsPostureMd: Expect targeted migration work, but continue reviewing individual breaks. Use less-breaking designs where they do not preserve obsolete or conflicting models indefinitely.
